assessment.nobel_worthiness: The legal-origins research program made investor protection and institutions central to comparative finance and development, with unusually broad scholarly and policy influence.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes and Shleifer form the core empirical and conceptual collaboration; the four-person formulation also recognizes Vishny, making a three-person award necessarily incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The central findings have been influential for decades and generated an extensive subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation of legal-origin comparisons remains contested.
A three-person limit leaves difficult credit allocation within the broader collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and financial-accelerator mechanisms supplied a durable framework for understanding amplification between finance and macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are central to the collateral-constraint formulation, while Gertler is central to the financial-accelerator line; the candidate's broader credit includes other indispensable contributors.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have been deeply incorporated into macro-finance research and became especially salient after repeated financial crises.
uncertainties: The contribution spans related mechanisms rather than one sharply bounded discovery.
Bernanke and other important contributors are outside the listed credit set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods transformed empirical work with longitudinal microdata by providing practical responses to endogeneity and fixed-effects problems.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are directly associated with the foundational estimator, and Blundell's joint work was central to the system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: These methods have been used and scrutinized across economics for many years.
uncertainties: Routine application has sometimes exceeded the conditions under which the estimators perform well.
The contribution may be viewed as a major methodological advance rather than a broad economic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining provided a simple, rigorous and highly portable account of bargaining outcomes and shaped modern game theory.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the unmistakable principal originator of the alternating-offers model; Wolinsky and Binmore represent important related work on bargaining and markets.
assessment.maturity: The model has remained a basic reference point for theoretical and applied bargaining research for decades.
uncertainties: The candidate combines a canonical core model with a wider body of related bargaining work.
Its abstraction can limit direct empirical interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made structural estimation of forward-looking decision problems operational and influential across applied fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust's foundational framework is especially clear; Keane and Eckstein made major contributions to subsequent development and application.
assessment.maturity: The approach has had long-lasting methodological impact and a large applied literature.
uncertainties: Computational and specification choices can make structural conclusions model-dependent.
Credit for the wider dynamic-choice literature extends beyond the listed names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work established management practices and organizational capital as measurable determinants of firm productivity, with consequences for policy and business organization.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen initiated the central measurement program, and Sadun has been a leading collaborator in its extension and validation.
assessment.maturity: The research has accumulated evidence across countries and organizations and has influenced work on firms and productivity.
uncertainties: Measurement and causality remain challenging because management practices co-vary with many firm characteristics.
The field is younger and less settled than the highest-ranked foundational contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on credit risk, over-the-counter market structure and search gave finance tractable models of illiquid decentralized markets with clear relevance during stress episodes.
assessment.attribution: Duffie, Pedersen and Garleanu made distinct but strongly complementary contributions to the theory of search, intermediation and asset-market liquidity.
assessment.maturity: The work has had substantial influence in finance and informs analysis of market design and regulation.
uncertainties: The discovery label combines several adjacent contributions.
Empirical measurement of the mechanisms and their aggregate importance remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of household leverage and mortgage credit materially changed understanding of how credit booms and balance-sheet distress affect aggregate demand.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are central to the empirical household-debt program; Campbell's work provides foundational analysis of household finance and mortgage choice.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has been extensively discussed following the global financial crisis and remains central to macro-finance.
uncertainties: Separating debt-driven mechanisms from local shocks and housing-price movements is empirically demanding.
The appropriate boundary between this work and the wider household-finance literature is not fully settled.
